clue.text: Pinched hired article of clothing

parts.note: pinched as in drawn and thin in the face
a room that is let has been hired out

explanation.surface: Someone has stolen a garment they had only rented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' reads as stolen, but here it means haggard and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a heavy protective glove, so it is a worn item of dress.

clue.text: 9-0 to us — splendid!

parts.note: the answer to 9 down is a canyon, which is a gorge
the figure zero reads as the letter O
us taken as written; to joins it on

explanation.surface: A nine-nil win for our side: wonderful!
explanation.walkthrough: 9-0 looks like a football score; 9 refers to the answer at 9 down, and 0 is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgeous means beautiful or magnificent, a close synonym of splendid.

clue.text: 19 valuers in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it is part of the fodder as well as the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: A team of global valuers has fallen into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The in of in disarray does double duty: its letters join valuers as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal and global both mean applying everywhere, to the whole world.

clue.text: Strip right away from the crowd

indicators.note: away from means leaving, so a letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: a throng is a crowd
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone undresses on the spot, away from the onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip looks like a verb, to undress; it is a noun, a narrow piece of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a lace, whip or strap.

clue.text: Formerly over-coloured, but not burning now

parts.note: ex means former, finished and over
tinct is an old word for tinged or coloured

explanation.surface: Something once too brightly dyed has now stopped burning.
explanation.walkthrough: Over-coloured looks like garish; split it, and over belongs with formerly.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct fire or volcano has gone out and is no longer alight or active.

clue.text: National spirit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to a nation, here Scotland
second meaning: whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: A country's drink, or the collective mood of a people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National spirit' looks like patriotic feeling; it is two separate meanings, an adjective of nationality and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is the adjective for things of Scotland, and also the everyday name for Scottish whisky.

clue.text: Carpet — one laid between players and spectators

indicators.note: laid between means set in the middle, so this piece sits between the other two in sequence

parts.note: the cast is the players in a production
the Roman numeral for one
the gate is the number of spectators at a match

explanation.surface: A rug has been put down between the stage and the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet looks like a floor covering, but to carpet someone is British slang for scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet an employee is to haul them in for a severe telling-off, which is to castigate them.

clue.text: Supernatural Scandinavian fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a giant or dwarf of Norse folklore
second meaning: a verb, to angle by trailing a line

explanation.surface: A magical fish from the waters of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish reads as a noun describing the Scandinavian creature; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a cave-dwelling creature of Norse myth, and to troll is to fish with a moving baited line.

clue.text: Make saint Henry sound like an ox

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: sound like tells the solver to go by how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: an ox makes a low, its deep call

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to canonise someone called Henry by making him moo.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is the physics unit, symbol H; what an ox utters is a low.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to make holy or sanctify, which is what making someone a saint does.

clue.text: Caught somebody, having dropped the last in the gully

indicators.note: dropping the last means losing the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
anyone means any person, somebody

explanation.surface: A fielder caught someone, then dropped the final catch in the gully.
explanation.walkthrough: Gully is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman, but here it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep steep-sided valley, a larger kind of gully or gorge.

clue.text: He's liable to charge cash

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an animal known for charging at intruders
second meaning: old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who will bill you for things in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests billing a customer, but it is the beast's headlong run. Rhino is dated British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is famous for stampeding at threats, and rhino is an old slang word for ready money.

clue.text: Fungus withstood a lot, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in an order not given

parts.note: split into two words, with stood: with is only the joining word, and stood is the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough fungus has survived a great deal of hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read withstood as 'with stood': with is the link, and stood a lot is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom-like growth, usually an inedible or poisonous kind of fungus.

clue.text: Crisis when Eastern quarter conceals information

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to give no quarter is to show no mercy
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A crisis breaks out when one eastern district withholds intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarter reads as a district of a city; here it is clemency shown to a beaten enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden serious situation that needs immediate action, much the same as a crisis.

clue.text: One must have leave to look inside the White House

definitions.note: a cryptic description: a house built of white snow

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other, splitting the outer word

parts.note: to go is to leave
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Visitors need a pass to see inside the American president's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The White House here is not in Washington: it is a house that is white because it is made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome house built from blocks of snow, so it is literally a white house.

clue.text: Parvenu puts faked pictures on show

indicators.note: something faked has been rigged up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
pictures on display in a gallery are art

explanation.surface: A social climber exhibits forged paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faked pictures' wants to be forged art, but faked works only on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone newly risen to wealth or status, which is exactly what an upstart is called.

clue.text: Colour that's fashionable for interior decoration of French hostelry

indicators.note: interior decoration of something goes inside it, so one piece is placed within

parts.note: auberge is the French word for an inn
what is in is fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy paint shade is chosen to decorate the inside of a French inn.
explanation.walkthrough: Interior decoration suggests paint and wallpaper; it means placing one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is a dark purple shade named after the skin of the eggplant.

clue.text: Slight difference is not apparent in pest

indicators.note: if a word is not apparent in another it is missing from it, so it is taken away

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance
taken as written; these are the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Two pests look almost identical: the difference cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of NUISANCE and NUANCE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or tone, a small distinction between things.

clue.text: Dry up about celebration — first find a place to eat …

indicators.note: first says the pieces after it come at the front, ahead of the other one

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
a fete is a festive celebration

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it

explanation.surface: Mop up after the party, then go and get some food.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots run the clue on into 18 down. Dry up is not one phrase: dry is the word, up turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant where diners collect their food, so it is a place to eat.

clue.text: … being hungry, and keen on several eggs

parts.note: a keen blade is sharp
a set of eggs is a clutch laid for a hen to sit on

explanation.surface: Continuing 17: someone famished and eager for a plate of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Keen on reads as fond of; split it, and on joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old word for ravenous, with appetite sharpened by hunger.

clue.text: Make ball go spinning around the world

indicators.note: to make is to form something new, so the letters are formed into a fresh order
spinning things whirl round and lose their order, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Set a ball spinning so it travels right round the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Go looks like part of the instruction, but its letters join ball as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something global extends throughout the whole planet, so it reaches around the world.

clue.text: Stir jam with more vigour

parts.note: a wheel that jams locks
to step something up is to give it more energy

explanation.surface: A cook is told to beat the preserves harder.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir and jam look like kitchen words; stir is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is a slang term for a jail, and a lock-up is a small prison or cell.

clue.text: Shakespearian knight, we hear, can be glorious

definitions.note: completes the play title Twelfth Night, knight being heard as night
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word before Night in a Shakespeare comedy title, knight standing in for its sound-twin
second meaning: the Glorious ___, a British date

explanation.surface: A knight in a Shakespeare play is said to be capable of glory.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night is Shakespeare's comedy; the Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when the British grouse-shooting season opens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word fills both phrases: the play Twelfth Night and the Glorious Twelfth of August in Britain.

clue.text: Bar for high fliers

parts.note: surface reading: a pub or club reserved for the very successful
setter's reading: circus acrobats who swing far above the ring

explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a place to drink, and high fliers the high achievers; it is a swinging bar for aerialists.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal pole hung on ropes that circus acrobats swing from.

clue.text: Despite having money, keep quiet about it

indicators.note: about it means going around the thing just named, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: whist is an old call for silence, like hush
L stands for pound, as in the old pounds-shillings-pence

explanation.surface: Rich as you are, say nothing of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite having money' reads as one phrase, but having just links: despite is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst can mean although, as in 'whilst I sympathise, I disagree', the same concessive sense as despite.

clue.text: One who has to talk nonsense!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a holder or possessor of something
second meaning: a Scottish verb for babbling foolishly

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to speak rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has to' reads as must; split it after has, and to begins the second definition. To haver is Scots for to blather.
explanation.definitionFit: A haver is literally a person who possesses, and in Scots to haver means to chatter foolishly.

clue.text: Perhaps it's under rocket attack

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts this piece below the other one

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible version, so the letters come in some other order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A target comes under bombardment from missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1, read as VI, was the flying bomb launched against London in 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit can mean to afflict or inflict, as when a plague visits a city, so it can mean to attack.

clue.text: Figure included in rent bill

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits within it, so a piece is placed inside

parts.note: to charter a boat or plane is to rent it
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A sum shown on a landlord's invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure and bill both suggest money; figure is the definition, a person in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure in a novel or a painting is a character, a person who appears in it.

clue.text: Liquor — doctor interjected "Take it slowly"

indicators.note: to interject is to throw something in between, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: ale is a beer, an alcoholic liquor
MB is the degree Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor warns a drinker to go easy on the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: Take it slowly looks like the doctor's advice, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow relaxed pace, taking one's time.

clue.text: Details us off for fatigue

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rota assigns us leave because we are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Details reads as a verb, assigning us to duty; it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental weariness, the same as fatigue.

clue.text: Brooke's said to be a poet

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the possessive name is taken by its sound, as a plural noun

parts.note: spoken, the name is brooks, small streams, and in Scotland a stream is called by this other word

explanation.surface: Rupert Brooke is said to be a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooke the poet is a decoy; spoken, Brooke's is brooks, small streams, which in Scotland are burns. Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns, author of Auld Lang Syne, is the most famous Scottish poet.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily in summer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stagger or wobble
second meaning: one who sums, adding figures up

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about in the hot season.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer is not the season: read it as sum-mer, a person who adds up, who tots.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to move shakily, and a totter is one who tots up columns of numbers.

clue.text: Welsh engineers first to make bearing

definitions.note: an adjective: having bearing on the matter

indicators.note: first tells the solver to put this piece at the front, ahead of the other one

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to welsh is to run off without paying a debt, which is also to levant

explanation.surface: Engineers from Wales lead the way in fixing a bearing for a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh looks like nationality but is the verb for dodging a debt; levant is the old word for the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relevant has a bearing on the question, being connected and pertinent to it.
